newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hutchison Port sees strong growth in 2nd half.
newsitem.headline: Hutchison Port sees strong growth in 2nd half.

text.p: Hutchison Port Holdings, a wholly owned subsidiary of Hutchison Whampoa Ltd, sees strong business growth in the second half of the year after Hong Kong hands over its sovereignty to China, John Meredith, group managing director of Hutchison Port, said on Thursday.
"The company never makes forecasts of growth but I think it will be very satisfactory (for this year)," Meredith told reporters.
"We are looking for very strong growth after July when the changes have taken effect," he said, adding that confidence will draw in investment.
Hutchison Port, a major port operator in Hong Kong, owns a number of container ports in Hong Kong's Kwai Chung through its subsidiary Hong Kong International Terminals.
The managing director also said the company's Hong Kong port charges had gone up only about one-third of the actual annual inflation rate but he declined to give a precise figure.
Hong Kong's shipping and port services have been hit by a slow down of cross-border trade with China.
Hutchison Port also has interests in various China terminals in Shanghai, Shenzhen, Golan, Nanhai, Jiangman and Xiamen.
